candidates.title: Anne Imhof
candidates.blurb: Imhof's first solo institutional show in Asia positions her durational performance practice within Hong Kong's colonial-turned-cultural heritage site.

candidates.title: Isaac Chong Wai: An Intimate Surrender
candidates.blurb: Solo show by Hong Kong-born, Berlin-based performance artist known for endurance works examining state power and bodily resistance.
candidates.why_shortlisted: Hong Kong diaspora artist addressing site history

candidates.title: Alicja Kwade: Waiting Pavilions
candidates.blurb: Kwade's mirrored sculptures placed in a former colonial prison yard create unexpected geometries between incarceration and public space.

candidates.title: Treasures of Global Jewellery from The Metropolitan Museum of Art: The Body Transformed
candidates.blurb: The Met's global ornament collection examined through adornment as social signaling, arriving as Hong Kong recalibrates luxury codes post-mainland integration.

candidates.title: Ancient Egypt Unveiled: Treasures from Egyptian Museums
candidates.blurb: Egyptian state collections staged in a museum built to project China's imperial continuity, a rare non-Western cultural loan to Beijing's institutional proxy.

candidates.title: The Hong Kong Jockey Club Series: Treasures of the Mughal Court from the Victoria and Albert Museum
candidates.blurb: V&A Mughal holdings shown alongside Palace Museum objects trace parallel imperial aesthetics of display and conquest.

candidates.title: Wonders of Imperial Carpets: Masterpieces from the Museum of Islamic Art, Doha
candidates.blurb: Doha loans Islamic carpets to a museum built on Palace Museum ties, mapping Gulf–China cultural diplomacy through decorative arts.

candidates.title: A Movable Feast: The Culture of Food and Drink in China
candidates.blurb: Palace Museum tableware and ritual vessels presented as a history of Chinese gastronomy, locating culture through consumption.

candidates.title: The Forbidden City and The Palace of Versailles: China-France Cultural Encounters in the Seventeenth and Eighteenth Centuries
candidates.blurb: Dual-court exchange objects trace early modern East-West visual translation, staged as soft power precedent for contemporary Sino-European relations.

candidates.title: Joyful Encounters: The Connoisseurship and Art of Wong Kwan Shut
candidates.blurb: Solo show on a Hong Kong scholar-collector whose taste shaped local literati networks, rare institutional acknowledgment of the city's curatorial genealogy.
candidates.why_shortlisted: Hong Kong collecting history, local connoisseurship

candidates.title: A History of China in Silk: The Chris Hall Collection at the Hong Kong Palace Museum
candidates.blurb: Western collector's Chinese textiles return home via Hong Kong, charting how expatriate connoisseurship built the market for imperial material culture.

candidates.title: Blooming: The Art of Gardens in East and West
candidates.blurb: Comparative study of garden aesthetics reads landscape design as cultural ideology through Chinese scholar rocks and European formal planning.

candidates.title: Fermata: Hong Kong in Venice Collateral Event of the 61st International Art Exhibition – La Biennale di Venezia
candidates.blurb: Venice Biennale collateral presentation returns to Hong Kong, test case for how the city frames its art internationally then displays it locally.

candidates.title: Live: Hong Kong Art Exhibition
candidates.blurb: Survey of contemporary Hong Kong artists working across media, state institution's attempt to define what counts as local art now.
candidates.why_shortlisted: Hong Kong art definition, institutional survey

candidates.title: Proudly from Canton: The Muwen Tang Collection of Cantonese and Export Art
candidates.blurb: Cantonese export art shown as regional identity assertion, curatorial nod to southern Chinese visual culture distinct from Beijing's narrative.
